transcript.text: Influence, the psychology of persuasion.
>> Five out of five fire emojis. It lays
the basis of changing behavior of both
internally and externally to companies,
so with customers and team. Super
beneficial for building sales processes,
less than sales scripts.
>> How to win friends and influence people.
Five out of five flex your arm emojis.
Very clear in terms of what to do to
change your behavior to get more people
to like you and do what you would prefer
them do. I've read it a bunch. There's
not many books I've read many, many
times. That is one of them. Like it's
one of the few books where I think to
myself, if I only did 100% of everything
in this book every single time, I would
guarantee success in life. It's just
very hard to do.
>> 50 scientifically proven ways to be
persuasive.
>> Love this book. Super
underrated. 10 out of five fire ball
emojis. This was the first book that I
ever read in persuasion and I think it
was Cialdini's early work before he
built into the the pillars of influence,
but because it's just like little
tactics that work, I've used so many of
those things in my life from the moment
I read the book.
>> What's probably your non-Cialdini
favorite book on persuasion?
>> I'm going to answer with an
untraditional answer, On Writing by
Stephen King, because I think if you
learn how to write, you learn how to
think. If you learn how to think, you
can advertise because you can keep
things simple and compelling. Simple
sells.
